rationale_short: Vendor names KYT product for "Monitor transactions in real-time" and 2025 Chainalysis Crypto Crime Report (analyst) attests FBI's use of Chainalysis tracing in DMM heist attribution (T_indep).
SoK narrative lists "Graph, Attribution" as Chainalysis technical approach and vendor cites "hundreds of clustering heuristics" but neither names a specific GNN architecture (T_indep narrative).
No mention of zero-knowledge proofs in any Chainalysis vendor pages or cross-platform sources covering P01.
No MEV detection product or strategy categories named in Chainalysis vendor pages or third-party sources.
Vendor names KYT as a real-time screening product and Reactor as investigation tool but no specific endpoint family or authentication scheme is documented (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Vendor describes HALO "transaction monitoring" detecting "spoofing, layering/quote stuffing" via real-time detection, corroborated by Solidus 2023 wash-trade report quantifying $2B detected on Ethereum DEXes (T_indep analyst).
Solidus vendor pages describe behavioral analytics and ML but no GNN architecture is named, and no peer-reviewed paper benchmarks Solidus's GNN.
Solidus Labs vendor pages describe market surveillance and HALO platform but make no Travel Rule claim and no FATF/regulator source associates Solidus with Travel Rule.
Solidus is a market-surveillance platform with no W3C VC/DID/attestation credential layer mentioned in any source.
Solidus vendor materials describe wash-trade and market-abuse detection but do not name MEV strategies (sandwich, JIT, arbitrage), and no T_indep paper attributes MEV analysis to Solidus.

Vendor names Lossless Aegis for "threat monitoring and smart contract defense" with "Automated real-time freezing of suspicious transactions" but no T_indep source corroborates the monitoring pipeline (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).

Vendor claims DeFi-focused protection across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon, BSC, etc. but does not name specific DeFi protocols (Uniswap, Aave, Compound) labeled with semantics (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).
Lossless vendor page describes exploit prevention but does not mention MEV strategies or front-running protection by name.
Lossless vendor page describes a token-standard LERC-20 and community-flagging mechanism but no REST/GraphQL/SDK API for programmatic access.
Lossless vendor materials describe community-stake-based reporting and freezing logic with no ML or GNN claim.

Vendor describes Veriscope as "The only frictionless Crypto Travel Rule compliance solution" with VASP discovery and PII transfer, and the Notabene 2024 Travel Rule survey lists Shyft among the Travel Rule platforms operating across 70+ jurisdictions (T_indep analyst).
Vendor describes Shyft as a "global attestation and governance platform" with patented attestation mechanisms but no W3C VC or DID schema is explicitly named (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).
Shyft vendor pages focus on identity attestations and Travel Rule messaging; no transaction-monitoring product, alert categories, or rule families are documented.

Vendor describes "OAuth2-type interface for Web 2.0 and 3.0 applications" enabling VASP-to-VASP data transfer but no REST/GraphQL endpoint family or authentication scheme is named (T_vendor) (vendor-only evidence).
Shyft Network is an identity/Travel Rule infrastructure with no MEV detection capability mentioned in any source.

Vendor names "Suspicious Transaction Activity Reporting (STAR)" and "Suspicious Activity Monitoring (SAM)" as discrete AML products, and DOJ Binance settlement (T_indep regulator) names mandatory SAR filing obligations under 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) which NICE Actimize products fulfill.

Vendor names "Currency Transaction Reporting (CTR)" and sanctions screening as named jurisdictional reports, and FinCEN CVC-mixing NPR (T_indep regulator) substantiates U.S. CTR/SAR-style reporting demand.

Vendor names "Suspicious Activity Monitoring (SAM)" product and homepage claims "5 billion+ transactions monitored daily," with explicit ML+rule-based methodology (T_vendor with corroborating SoK narrative classifying NICE Actimize as Tx Monitoring T_indep).
NICE Actimize vendor materials describe ML and "entity-centric" AML but no GNN architecture (GCN, GraphSAGE, etc.) is named, and no T_indep source benchmarks an Actimize GNN.
NICE Actimize is a traditional-AML platform with chain coverage L0; no Travel Rule capability is documented in any vendor or cross-platform source.
